audit.whatIsWrong: The packet chart cannot be trusted here and the packet says so itself: "level chart contradicts data: Zaahen wins only 46.41% but the chart gives Zaahen 4/7 stages vs 0". Meanwhile the content whys[1], whys[2] and whys[5] claim Zaahen wins levels 2, 3 and first item while the sides on both layers say Heimerdinger.
audit.why: Zaahen is at 46.41% over 306 games — he loses this lane. The mirror audit resolved it the same way: it rewrote whys[1], whys[2] and whys[5] to Heimerdinger's side to match the stored chart, and flipped only row 6 to Zaahen. So the stored sides are right for rows 1, 2 and 5 and the prose was wrong; row 6 is the single genuine flip.
audit.corrected: Row 6 flipped to Zaahen in both layers as a matched pair with its rating. whys[1], whys[2] and whys[5] rewritten to Heimerdinger's side so the prose stops contradicting the chart. I deliberately did NOT apply the packet chart — the packet flags itself as contradicting the win rate, and following it would put the two directions of this matchup in direct conflict.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and the whole page is built on "clear his turrets, then engage" — which the numbers do not support.
audit.why: H-28 G Evolution Turret is a 1-second cooldown at 20 mana. Clearing turrets is not a window you can open; he re-places faster than you can remove them, and the page's core instruction is therefore wrong in kind, not just in detail. The real windows are CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade on a flat 11s and Hextech Micro-Rockets on 11/10/9/8/7 from 1325 range. UPGRADE!!! is 100/85/70 against Grim Deliverance's 110/95/80.
audit.corrected: Turret's 1s/20-mana economy stated so the player stops trying to win a clearing war, and the Grenade's flat 11s made the actual thing to bait.

audit.whatIsWrong: (a) "Golden Onslaught" (Aureate Rush) and "Final Retribution" (Grim Deliverance) again, plus "Darkin Glaive" for The Darkin Glaive. (b) The Grenade is treated as an all-or-nothing stun; the kit says it stuns "anyone directly hit" and only slows surrounding units. (c) Hextech Affinity is absent from the page entirely.
audit.why: The direct-hit-only stun is the sequencing fact this matchup needs: stepping off the centre of the grenade downgrades his self-peel to a slow, which is the difference between reaching him and not. Hextech Affinity granting move speed near his turrets explains why he kites you so well inside his nest and why the fight has to happen outside it — the page says "dive his nest" in four fields, which is the opposite instruction.
audit.corrected: Real names used, direct-hit-versus-edge stated, Hextech Affinity's move speed named as the reason to fight off the nest, and Determination's revive added to the late-game text.

notes: I did NOT apply the packet level chart here. The packet flags itself: it gives Zaahen 4 of 7 stages on a 46.41% win rate, and the mirror audit resolved the same conflict by keeping Heimerdinger on rows 1, 2 and 5 and flipping only row 6. Following the packet would have put the two directions of this matchup in open disagreement and mirror-fix.js would have overwritten it anyway. The deeper problem is that the page's whole strategy — 'clear his turrets then engage', 'dive his nest', stated across tldr, winCon, report[0], report[1], spikes[0], early and wants.you[0] — is built on a false premise: the turret is a 1-second, 20-mana cooldown, so there is no clearing window to exploit. I rewrote the fields I could reach inside the length band; the short tldr/winCon/report strings still say 'dive his nest' and need a hand pass. Same recurring Zaahen fabrications: 'Golden Onslaught' and 'Final Retribution', now in six of six matchups.
